Bacterial Leaf Blight.description: A devastating bacterial disease causing wilting, yellowing, and death of plant tissue.
Bacterial Leaf Blight.causes: Spreads via water (rain/irrigation) and mechanical transfer in hot, humid conditions.
Bacterial Leaf Blight.prevention: Apply copper-based bactericides. Improve field drainage and avoid excessive nitrogen.

Apple Scab.description: A fungal disease that causes olive-green to black scabs on leaves and fruit.
Apple Scab.causes: Triggered by the fungus Venturia inaequalis, thriving in cool, wet spring weather.
Apple Scab.prevention: Rake and destroy fallen leaves. Apply protective fungicides early in the season.

Black Rot.description: A destructive fungal disease that causes brown circular lesions and rotting fruit.
Black Rot.causes: Caused by the fungus Guignardia bidwellii, spreading via rain splash from infected mummies.
Black Rot.prevention: Prune out diseased wood. Remove all mummified fruit and apply preventative fungicides.

Cedar Apple Rust.description: A complex fungal disease that requires two hosts (Juniper and Apple) causing orange-yellow spots.
Cedar Apple Rust.causes: Spores travel via wind from infected cedar/juniper trees during wet spring conditions.
Cedar Apple Rust.prevention: Remove nearby cedar/juniper hosts. Apply preventative sterol inhibitor fungicides.

Blight.description: A rapid and complete chlorosis, browning, and death of plant tissues (leaves, branches, flowers).
Blight.causes: Caused by various fungi and bacteria that thrive in warm, highly humid environments.
Blight.prevention: Increase air circulation through pruning. Apply broad-spectrum fungicides/bactericides.

Early Blight.description: Fungal disease causing 'bullseye' target-like dark spots starting on lower foliage.
Early Blight.causes: Alternaria solani fungus spreading from soil debris during warm, wet weather.
Early Blight.prevention: Rotate crops and use drip irrigation to keep leaves dry. Apply chlorothalonil-based treatments.

Late Blight.description: Highly aggressive disease causing large, dark, water-soaked lesions that rapidly kill the plant.
Late Blight.causes: Phytophthora infestans (a water mold) spreading via wind in cool, damp conditions.
Late Blight.prevention: Destroy all infected plants immediately. Use resistant varieties and robust fungicide programs.

Brown Spot.description: A common fungal disease characterized by small, circular brown/black spots surrounded by yellow halos.
Brown Spot.causes: Associated with poor soil fertility, plant stress, and extended periods of leaf wetness.
Brown Spot.prevention: Improve soil nutrition (especially NPK balance). Remove infected lower leaves.

Cercospora Leaf Spot.description: Fungal infection causing distinct gray-centered spots with purple to reddish-brown borders.
Cercospora Leaf Spot.causes: Spreads rapidly in prolonged high humidity and warm temperatures.
Cercospora Leaf Spot.prevention: Use pathogen-free seeds. Practice 2-3 year crop rotation and deep plowing of residue.

Powdery Mildew.description: Fungal disease that forms a distinct white, powdery coating on leaf surfaces and stems.
Powdery Mildew.causes: High humidity combined with dry foliage and moderate temperatures.
Powdery Mildew.prevention: Improve airflow via spacing. Apply sulfur-based or potassium bicarbonate fungicides.

Common Rust.description: Fungal disease identifiable by raised, reddish-brown pustules predominantly on leaf surfaces.
Common Rust.causes: Fungal spores transported by wind currents, requiring surface moisture to germinate.
Common Rust.prevention: Plant rust-resistant hybrids. Apply foliar fungicides at early detection stages.

Esca Black Measles.description: A complex wood disease causing 'tiger-stripe' leaf necrosis and spotting on fruit.
Esca Black Measles.causes: A complex of several fungi infecting through pruning wounds over multiple years.
Esca Black Measles.prevention: Practice sanitary pruning, protect large wounds with sealants, and remove infected wood.

Leaf Blight Isariopsis Leaf Spot.description: Fungal disease causing large, irregular brown patches that dry out and tear.
Leaf Blight Isariopsis Leaf Spot.causes: Fungus overwintering in plant debris and spreading during humid, rainy weather.
Leaf Blight Isariopsis Leaf Spot.prevention: Clean up all fallen leaf debris in autumn. Apply appropriate organic or chemical fungicides.

Gray Leaf Spot.description: Fungal infection causing small, tan, rectangular lesions restricted by leaf veins.
Gray Leaf Spot.causes: Cercospora zeae-maydis fungus surviving in crop residue, favored by overcast, humid days.
Gray Leaf Spot.prevention: Utilize crop rotation and tillage to bury residue. Select resistant plant genetics.

Leaf Smut.description: Fungal disease creating small, linear black blisters (smuts) filled with spores.
Leaf Smut.causes: Fungus overwinters in soil and residue, infecting new growth during wet weather.
Leaf Smut.prevention: Use certified disease-free seeds and utilize systemic seed treatments.

Nitrogen Deficiency.description: Nutrient disorder causing overall pale green to yellowing (chlorosis) of older leaves.
Nitrogen Deficiency.causes: Depleted soil nitrogen, poor root health, or excessive watering leaching nutrients.
Nitrogen Deficiency.prevention: Apply nitrogen-rich organic or synthetic fertilizers. Test soil pH to ensure nutrient availability.

Orange Haunglongbing Citrus Greening.description: Fatal bacterial disease causing mottled leaves, stunted growth, and bitter, green fruit.
Orange Haunglongbing Citrus Greening.causes: Transmitted exclusively by the Asian citrus psyllid insect vector.
Orange Haunglongbing Citrus Greening.prevention: No cure exists. Remove and destroy infected trees immediately. Control the psyllid vector population.

Bacterial Spot.description: Bacterial disease causing small, water-soaked spots that turn dark brown and angular.
Bacterial Spot.causes: Xanthomonas bacteria spreading via splashing rain, tools, and human contact.
Bacterial Spot.prevention: Avoid working with wet plants. Apply copper fungicides prophylactically.

Leaf Mold.description: Fungal disease starting as pale green spots on upper leaves with olive-green fuzzy mold underneath.
Leaf Mold.causes: Passalora fulva fungus flourishing in poorly ventilated environments with >85% humidity.
Leaf Mold.prevention: Maximize air circulation. Prune lower foliage and manage greenhouse humidity.

Healthy.description: Plant exhibits normal growth patterns, rich coloration, and no visual anomalies.
Healthy.causes: Optimal environmental conditions, robust soil microbiome, and excellent care.
Healthy.prevention: Continue current irrigation, fertilization, and monitoring practices.

Rot.description: Fungal or bacterial degradation of plant tissue often accompanied by a foul odor or mushy texture.
Rot.causes: Excessive moisture, poor drainage, and pathogens entering through mechanical wounds.
Rot.prevention: Drastically reduce moisture. Prune out all rotting tissue with sterile tools and improve airflow.

Spot.description: Localized lesions of dead tissue indicating localized fungal or bacterial infection.
Spot.causes: Water splashing pathogens from soil onto leaves, combined with poor airflow.
Spot.prevention: Switch to base-drip irrigation to keep leaves dry. Apply preventative broad-spectrum sprays.

Blight.description: Rapid, aggressive browning and dieback of plant tissue.
Blight.causes: Highly contagious fungal/bacterial spores thriving in humid micro-climates.
Blight.prevention: Quarantine affected plants immediately. Clear debris and implement an aggressive fungicide regimen.

Rust.description: Fungal infection creating powdery, orange/brown/yellow raised pustules.
Rust.causes: Wind-borne spores requiring extended periods of leaf wetness to establish.
Rust.prevention: Plant resistant cultivars. Maximize plant spacing to ensure rapid leaf drying after rain.

Mildew.description: Fungal growth appearing as a powdery or downy white/gray coating.
Mildew.causes: High humidity, overcrowded planting, and poor air circulation.
Mildew.prevention: Prune selectively to open the canopy. Apply sulfur or potassium bicarbonate treatments.

Deficiency.description: Physiological disorder due to lack of essential macro or micro nutrients.
Deficiency.causes: Depleted soil, incorrect pH locking out nutrients, or damaged root systems.
Deficiency.prevention: Conduct comprehensive soil testing. Apply targeted fertilizers and amend soil pH.
